body:
Design gets its own page in Solace, with **Architecture** and **UI/UX** tabs, and each design becomes a record that people and agents can cite and read. This is the base the other Design features sit on.

## Asked for

- One page with two tabs, not a tab in Strategy.
- Each design has an ID like a task's, written `design:<id>`, so agents can access it, refer to it and read it while working tasks.
- Design files live in the repo at least. Because designers may expect more than git gives them, the human is open to a local history with undo.
- Scope is the whole workspace, not one project. A workspace holds many designs, and a design may cover a small part of it or use components shared across projects.
- No text editor for humans (see vision: humans work without reading code).
- Eventually both tabs support drag and drop and WYSIWYG editing (feature: direct editing).
- Design sits between Strategy and Board in the menu.
- Each tab shows its designs in a flat list on the left side of the screen, and picking one shows it. How designs are grouped or arranged is decided later.

## Decided

- A design is **data, not code**. It stays out of the symbol store and the Gleam and Rust type checks.
- The **element** is the primitive: one component or container with a permanent ID.
- Solace validates a design with its own rules, such as known element types and properties, unique IDs and closed lists of values. A design that fails is not saved.
- A design is **reference material**; see the milestone.
- Build order for the first useful version: this feature, then UI/UX, then the design agent, then Architecture.

## Suggested (cursory, not prescriptive)

- **Current design in the repo, history in Solace's own data.** Each accepted change saves a version, and restoring one adds a new version, so later work isn't lost. As far as research showed, Figma's restore works this way, with automatic checkpoints, named versions and restore. What designers expect beyond this is uncertain.
- **Format:** not decided. JSON would suit, and humans never see it. Every file carries a schema version so the format can change later.
- **Page:** follow the existing page pattern, a Lustre app of its own registered by the shell, like D-85 and D-90, with `?tab=` tabs.
- **`design:<id>` links:** extend the `task:`, `feature:` and `milestone:` links (D-98, D-122), so a design link works in any Markdown and shows its title.
- **Agents' access:** design files would be watched by default (Spec 14 §1), so agents could write them directly and skip the visual check. They need a restriction like the human-approved writes on protected files.
- **Assumption:** each design lives on one tab.

## Open

- History in Solace's own data shares the open question of how task data reaches other developers (task:040fefdf07a5aeab). The current design in the repo travels with a clone; its history doesn't, because `.solace/` is ignored by git apart from `store.db` and `approved`. Left as is for now.
- Where a human sees a design's past versions and restores one.
- The other agent's plan kept an index of element IDs, pending proposals and history in a store. Only history and pending proposals clearly need storing; element IDs are already in the files.

## Not in this feature

Named versions, comparing versions, branches, and grouping or arranging designs.
title: design: page and records
